root_idea.summary: The root centers on violent motion, agitation, convulsion, and disturbance, whether physical or socially induced.
root_idea.development: The basic sense of physical quaking extends to trembling, rumbling, and other forms of agitation; Form IV also develops a causative social use in which speech produces public disturbance.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested active participle with the Form IV rumor-spreading sense.
Distinct Quran-attested substantivized feminine active participle in the Resurrection passage.
Distinct Quran-attested noun denoting a violent convulsion or earthquake.

senses.definition: To quake, tremble, or undergo violent agitation.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic imperfect active use, the subject is the earth, or the earth and mountains, in scenes of eschatological upheaval.

senses.definition: One who spreads false, discordant, or alarming reports that stir people into agitation.
senses.usage_conditions: A Form IV active participle; in the Quranic construction it denotes people who generate public disturbance through untrue or destabilizing reports.

senses.definition: The quaking one; in the Resurrection passage, the first blast of the horn.
senses.usage_conditions: A substantivized feminine active participle. This is one classical interpretation of the referent in 79:6.

senses.definition: The formerly motionless bodies, such as the earth and mountains, when violently set in motion.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative interpretation of the referent in 79:6, connected with the Quranic description of the earth and mountains quaking.
In its Quranic occurrences, it denotes the severe convulsion that overtakes a people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be in motion, commotion, agitation, convulsion, or disturbance; to tremble or quake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to things such as a camel beneath a saddle, a tree moved by wind, a wabbling tooth, a hand or arm, or a heart agitated by fright.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of thunder, to make a repeated rumbling or confused noise in the clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive use with thunder as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a people or party, to prepare for war or battle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use applied to a group preparing for armed conflict.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a thing or person into motion, agitation, convulsion, or shivering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use, including causing someone to quake or shiver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be in commotion intransitively, or to cause another thing or person to enter a state of motion or agitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the physical-motion use of Form IV, distinct from its social use of spreading agitating reports.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to come in a state of fatigue with her ears flaccid and shaking them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use describing the camel's fatigued movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Commotion, agitation, or convulsion, especially a violent earthquake; also a vehement cry from heaven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also reported in Quranic interpretation for a punishment that befalls a people. This headword is kept distinct from رَجْفَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Put into a state of commotion; of clouds, in commotion with thunder or much water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or descriptive use, including the conventional collocation for turbulent clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sea, because of its commotion and agitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional epithet based on the sea's restless motion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Day of Resurrection; also the congregation of those who have risen.
A kind of jolting or shaking pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use for a manner of walking or riding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Moving or putting something into a state of motion or agitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also applied to a fever attended by quaking or shivering and, in the feminine, to a she-camel moving her head while walking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The spreading of false, discordant, or evil tales that stir people into disturbance; also such false or discordant rumors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun of Form IV can function as a substantive for the resulting tales or rumors.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The basin and ewer used in washing before and after a meal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized dual term referring to the utensils whose clashing sound signals the completion of the meal and prompts diners to rise.

cautions: رَاجِفَةٌ in 79:6 has two reported interpretations in the lexical evidence: the first Resurrection blast, or the earth and mountains set violently in motion.
The Lane-attested رَجْعَةٌ entry is retained as a separate classical headword and is not conflated with the Quranic noun رَجْفَةٌ.
